name: claims
title: WWII unit location claims
description: One row per claim. Same header in every file under data/claims/. Vocabulary-backed fields refer to keys in schema/vocabularies.json.

repeatedColumns.description: Columns repeated from the unit table on every claim row so that a claim file is readable on its own. The validator requires them to equal data/units.csv.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.description: Unique id of the claim, C0001 onward. One row is one claim ("this unit was here on this date"). Never reused.

fields.name: conflict_group_id
fields.description: Shared by rows that make competing claims about the same unit and event (G001...). Blank if no known conflict.

fields.name: claim_status
fields.description: preferred, alternate or disputed (see vocabulary).

fields.name: unit_id
fields.description: Stable unit key, NATION-TYPE-NUMBER+ECHELONLETTER (for example US-INF-029D). Must exist in data/units.csv and match the file name.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date of the claim, YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: theater
fields.description: Primary theater of the claim (see vocabulary).

fields.name: nationality
fields.description: Nationality of the unit: the `name` of a row of data/nationalities.csv (foreign key; US, UK, Canada, Germany, ... Allied). Repeated from data/units.csv (must equal it). Matches the data/claims/<nationality>/ folder in lowercase.

fields.name: unit_name
fields.description: Unit name only, for example "29th Infantry Division".

fields.name: echelon
fields.description: Organisational level (see vocabulary).

fields.name: branch
fields.description: Service or arm (see vocabulary).

fields.name: parent_unit_id
fields.description: Unit id (from data/units.csv) of the operational parent on this row's date: the formation the unit was attached to or operating under, otherwise its standing parent. Blank if the unit has no parent (top-level headquarters), or if no parent could be verified; in that case command_relationships holds one entry {"unit_id": null, "relationship": "unknown", "note": ...}. The organic parent, when different, is in command_relationships.

fields.name: command_relationships
fields.description: JSON list of command relationships on this row's date: [{"unit_id": "<unit id, or null only with relationship unknown>", "relationship": "organic|assigned|attached|unspecified_subordination|operational_control|administrative_control|supporting|coordinating|reserve|unknown", "effective_from": "YYYY-MM-DD (optional)", "effective_to": "YYYY-MM-DD, last day of the relationship (optional)", "date_basis": "order|assignment_table|narrative|inferred (optional)", "note": "<optional; required when unit_id is null>"}]. Allowed keys: unit_id, relationship, effective_from, effective_from_latest, ordered_date, effective_to, effective_to_earliest, effective_to_basis, date_basis, effective_time, effective_to_time, note. The name of the formation is not stored: it comes from units.csv (derived display name, see docs/methodology.md). An entry whose formation is not a unit in units.csv has unit_id null, relationship unknown and a note saying what is unknown. parent_unit_id is the operational parent on the row's date; the standing parent is recorded only here, as an organic, assigned or unspecified_subordination entry. Blank if nothing is recorded (a top-level headquarters).

fields.name: commander
fields.description: Commander on that date, rank and name as given by sources; "unknown" if not verified.

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: Decimal degrees WGS84.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: Decimal degrees WGS84.

fields.name: location_name
fields.description: Name of the place the coordinate refers to.

fields.name: location_represents
fields.description: What the point stands for (see vocabulary).

fields.name: precision_km
fields.description: Judgment estimate of the radius in km within which the unit probably was (banded).

fields.name: operation_id
fields.description: Key of the most specific operation, battle, phase or campaign the claim belongs to, in data/operations.csv (for example OP-EPSOM, or the campaign row OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE when no named operation applies). Its parent chain gives the campaign, the umbrella (Overlord) and the named operation; build/all_claims.csv carries these as derived columns. The claim's date should lie inside the operation's dates; a claim just outside needs a row in data/operation_exceptions.csv.

fields.name: composing_units
fields.description: Subordinate units, listed when first given or when they change; blank means unchanged from the unit's previous row; "unknown" means no data.

fields.name: established
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was formed.

fields.name: disestablished
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was disbanded.

fields.name: destroyed
fields.description: True on the row where the source says the unit was destroyed.

fields.name: confidence
fields.description: Numeric 0-1 confidence by rubric (see vocabulary).

fields.name: source
fields.description: URLs separated by " | " ending with the coordinate source note. Every row needs at least one URL.

fields.name: reference_ids
fields.description: Stored links to the references that support this claim: reference_ids from data/references_meta.csv (R###), separated by ";", in citation order. The source of truth for claim-to-reference links (build/claim_references.csv and the claims_count of data/references.csv are built from it). The URLs in `source` stay as the readable citation and must resolve to ids listed here. Every claim needs at least one; a claim at confidence 0.9 should have references from at least two different source families (warning). The role of a link (event, date, location, command_relationship, strength) is in data/claim_reference_roles.csv; a link with no row there is "general".

fields.name: source_locator
fields.description: Where in a reference the claim is supported, as "R398: p. 285, 289; R407: p. 36" (reference_id, then page, chapter or section), separated by ";". Only ids that are in reference_ids. Blank where the citation gives no page; nothing is guessed. Filled from URL fragments (#page285) of the original citation.

fields.name: event_type
fields.description: One primary event type (see vocabulary).

fields.name: current_activity
fields.description: Short phrase (about 120 characters at most) saying the one action the sources document for the unit on that date at that place; lower-case, free text. No inferred direction or result; extra detail goes in notes.

fields.name: engaged_with
fields.description: Enemy units fought on that date, nationality first, separated by "; ". Blank = no combat that day; "unknown" = combat with no opponent identified.

fields.name: strength_status
fields.description: Qualitative strength (see vocabulary).

fields.name: strength_json
fields.description: Optional JSON object with sourced strength figures: {"basis","as_of","personnel","vehicles","vehicle_count_type","scope","source","note"}; scope (whole_unit, sub_force, sector) says what the figure covers and is required whenever personnel is present. See docs/methodology.md. Blank where no source gives figures.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free text: what the source says, caveats, source conflicts, change history.

fields.name: location_date
fields.description: Optional. The date the coordinate is actually documented for, when it differs from date (for example the date of the command post list the point was taken from). Blank when the coordinate is for the claim's own date or the date is not known.

fields.name: location_basis
fields.description: Optional. How the coordinate relates in time and place to date (see vocabulary location_basis). Blank on rows not yet reviewed.

fields.name: location_temporal_offset_days
fields.description: Optional integer: location_date minus date in days (positive = coordinate is from a later date). Blank when location_date is blank.
